newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch Sphinx takes NLG 30 mln charge.
newsitem.headline: Dutch Sphinx takes NLG 30 mln charge.

text.p: Sanitaryware maker Sphinx said on Thursday it was setting aside 30 million guilders to restructure its Ceramic Sanitary Ware product group, focusing particularly on Germany.
"A provision of around NLG 30 million will be charged against the result of the current financial year in connection with the reorganisation," the company said in a statement.
It said the charge was expected to lead to a net loss of 15 million guilders over the current 1996/97 financial year, which ends on March 31.
"The planned reorganisation provision of NLG 30 million will have a substantial effect on the 1996/97 result," it said.

Price pressure and stock reductions throughout the year, coupled with sharply increased losses at Deutsche Sphinx and Belgian producers for the German sanitaryware market would lead to much lower net profits from ordinary activities, it said.
"This is expected to lead to...a subsequent loss of NLG 15 million," it said.
In November, the company said it expected to post a modest full-year profit over 1996/97.
Sphinx said the reorganisation would be aimed at structurally improving profitability at its Ceramic Sanitary Ware product group.

The restructuring would lead to "substantial" job losses in Belgium at its Warneton Industries and Novoboch factories, while its Wallhausen-based Deutsche Sphinx Sanitar factory would remain operational at a substantially lower capacity level.
The restructuring would help boost operating results, leading to a modest profit in 1997/98, it said.
Sphinx said it had been struggling with structural problems at Ceramic Sanitary Ware for some time, due mainly to difficult conditions in Germany and France which were pressuring margins and volumes.
The reorganisation would cut costs and reduce loss-making deliveries to customers, while the product range would also be slimmed down by more than 30 percent.

In addition some production would be contracted out to low-wage countries, it said, adding "the necessary capacity has already been secured." Eventually 20 percent of present turnover will be contracted out, Sphinx said.
